q: Which Y-chromosome gene starts testis development?
x: SRY, the sex-determining region of the Y chromosome, encodes testis-determining factor. It switches on SOX9 and makes the supporting cells of the gonad become Sertoli cells.

w.SOX9: SOX9 is an autosomal gene that SRY switches on. It carries out testis formation but sits downstream, not on the Y chromosome.
w.AMH gene: The AMH gene is an autosomal gene that SOX9 switches on in Sertoli cells. It acts after testis development has begun, not at the start.
w.5α-reductase gene: The 5α-reductase gene makes the enzyme that converts testosterone to DHT. It acts after the testis exists and does not start testis development.
w.Androgen receptor gene: The androgen receptor gene is on the X chromosome. It acts after the testis exists, when target tissues respond to testosterone and DHT.

pt.say: The first line of the male column reads SRY → testis-determining factor, the step that starts testis development.

q: Which fetal testis cells secrete anti-Müllerian hormone?
x: Sertoli cells, the first cells SRY creates, secrete anti-Müllerian hormone from about week 8, making the Müllerian duct on the same side regress. They also support the germ cells inside the testis cords.

w.Leydig cells: Leydig cells in the interstitium secrete testosterone under hCG stimulation, which keeps the Wolffian ducts but does not remove the Müllerian ducts.
w.Spermatogonia: Spermatogonia come from primordial germ cells that migrated in from the yolk sac. They are future gametes and secrete no duct hormone.
w.Granulosa cells: Granulosa cells are the ovarian counterpart of Sertoli cells. They are not in the fetal testis, and the fetal ovary makes little AMH.
w.Theca cells: Theca cells surround ovarian follicles and supply androgens. They are not in the fetal testis and make no AMH.

pt.say: The Sertoli cells → AMH box shows the source of anti-Müllerian hormone and its effect: the Müllerian ducts regress.

q: Which hormone preserves the Wolffian ducts in a male fetus?
x: Testosterone from fetal Leydig cells acts directly on the neighboring Wolffian ducts, which do not need DHT, turning them into the epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and ejaculatory duct.

w.Dihydrotestosterone: DHT builds the penis, scrotum and prostate. 5α-reductase deficiency leaves normal Wolffian ducts, proving that testosterone alone is enough for them.
w.Anti-Müllerian hormone: AMH removes the Müllerian ducts but does nothing to maintain the Wolffian ducts, which regress without androgen even when AMH is present.
w.Estradiol: Estradiol is not needed for duct development in either sex. The female ducts develop simply because AMH and testosterone are absent.
w.Inhibin B: Inhibin B from Sertoli cells feeds back on pituitary FSH after birth. It plays no part in keeping the fetal genital ducts.

pt.say: The Leydig cells → testosterone box shows testosterone keeping the Wolffian ducts that build the epididymis and vas deferens.

q: Which enzyme converts testosterone to DHT in genital skin?
x: 5α-reductase converts testosterone to the more potent DHT in the genital tubercle, folds, swellings and urogenital sinus. Its deficiency leaves a 46,XY infant undervirilized with normal Wolffian ducts.

w.Aromatase: Aromatase converts testosterone to estradiol. It lowers androgen potency instead of raising it.
w.17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase: 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase makes testosterone from androstenedione in Leydig cells, one step before the conversion that genital skin performs.
w.21-hydroxylase: 21-hydroxylase is an adrenal enzyme needed for cortisol and aldosterone. Its deficiency causes congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
w.Desmolase: Desmolase (cholesterol side-chain cleavage) is the first step of all steroid synthesis, converting cholesterol to pregnenolone.

pt.say: The bottom male box shows 5α-reductase → DHT, the conversion that builds the penis, scrotum and prostate.

q: Which embryonic duct forms the seminal vesicle?
x: The seminal vesicle buds from the caudal mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, which also forms the epididymis, vas deferens and ejaculatory duct. All four depend on testosterone and are remembered as SEED.

w.Paramesonephric duct: The paramesonephric duct regresses in males under anti-Müllerian hormone, leaving only the appendix testis as a remnant.
w.Urogenital sinus: The urogenital sinus forms the prostate, bulbourethral glands, bladder and urethra, glands that lie below the seminal vesicles.
w.Ureteric bud: The ureteric bud also sprouts from the mesonephric duct but forms the ureter and collecting system rather than a genital gland.
w.Allantois: The allantois becomes the urachus between the bladder and umbilicus and forms no part of the male genital tract.

pt.say: The Leydig cell box lists the Wolffian duct products, including the seminal vesicle; all come from the mesonephric duct.

q: Which female structure comes from the urogenital sinus rather than the Müllerian ducts?
x: The fused Müllerian ducts form the tubes, uterus, cervix and upper vagina, while the endodermal urogenital sinus forms the lower vagina. The two meet at the vaginal plate, which hollows out.

w.Upper vagina: The upper vagina comes from the fused lower ends of the Müllerian ducts, together with the cervix.
w.Cervix: The cervix forms from the fused lower Müllerian ducts, which is why complete fusion failure in didelphys gives two cervices.
w.Uterine fundus: The uterine body and fundus form where the Müllerian ducts fuse. Incomplete fusion there produces a bicornuate uterus.
w.Fallopian tube: The fallopian tubes are the unfused upper parts of the Müllerian ducts, not of the urogenital sinus.

pt.say: The bottom band separates the Müllerian ducts, which form the upper vagina, cervix, uterus and tubes, from the urogenital sinus, which forms the lower vagina.

q: A Gartner duct cyst is a remnant of which duct?
x: Without testosterone the mesonephric duct regresses in females, but remnants can persist along the lateral wall of the vagina and cervix and fill with fluid as a Gartner duct cyst.

w.Paramesonephric duct: The paramesonephric ducts do not regress in females. They form the tubes, uterus, cervix and upper vagina themselves.
w.Urachus: The urachus is the allantois remnant between bladder dome and umbilicus. Its cysts sit in the midline abdominal wall.
w.Vitelline duct: Vitelline duct remnants produce Meckel diverticulum or umbilical cysts along the path from midgut to umbilicus.
w.Thyroglossal duct: Thyroglossal duct cysts are midline neck masses that move with swallowing, left behind by the descending thyroid.

pt.say: In the female column the Wolffian ducts regress, with one remnant noted: a Gartner duct cyst from the mesonephric duct.

q: The labioscrotal swellings become which female structure?
x: Without DHT the labioscrotal swellings stay separate as the labia majora. In males DHT makes them fuse in the midline into the scrotum, which is why a bifid scrotum reflects incomplete fusion.

w.Labia minora: The labia minora come from the urogenital folds, the homologs of the ventral penile shaft and spongy urethra.
w.Clitoris: The clitoris comes from the genital tubercle, the same primordium that forms the glans and shaft of the penis.
w.Vestibule: The vestibule is the space between the labia minora, derived from the urogenital sinus, into which urethra and vagina open.
w.Hymen: The hymen is the membrane at the junction of the vaginal plate and urogenital sinus. Failure to perforate causes hematocolpos.

pt.say: Follow the labioscrotal swellings row to the right: in females they become the labia majora.

q: Failure of which embryonic fusion causes hypospadias?
x: Under DHT the urethral folds fuse along the underside of the phallus to enclose the spongy urethra. Incomplete fusion of the urethral folds leaves the opening on the ventral shaft, scrotum or perineum.

w.Labioscrotal swellings: Unfused labioscrotal swellings produce a bifid scrotum, which can accompany severe hypospadias but does not itself misplace the meatus.
w.Müllerian ducts: Failed Müllerian fusion produces uterine anomalies such as didelphys or a bicornuate uterus, not a penile defect.
w.Urorectal septum: The urorectal septum divides the cloaca into the urogenital sinus and the anorectal canal. Failure leaves a fistula with the rectum, not hypospadias.
w.Palatine shelves: Unfused palatine shelves produce a cleft palate. The process looks similar but belongs to the face, not the genitalia.

pt.say: The urogenital folds row shows these folds forming the ventral shaft and spongy urethra; unfused urethral folds leave hypospadias.

q: Which uterine anomaly is most common and most linked to recurrent miscarriage?
x: A septate uterus forms when the midline septum between the fused Müllerian ducts fails to resorb. The poorly vascularized septum is a poor implantation site, so this is the anomaly most linked to recurrent miscarriage.

w.Bicornuate uterus: A bicornuate uterus comes from partial failure of fusion and shows a deep external fundal cleft. It carries more preterm birth than early loss.
w.Uterus didelphys: Didelphys is complete fusion failure with two uteri and two cervices. It is rarer, and only sometimes comes with an obstructed hemivagina.
w.Unicornuate uterus: A unicornuate uterus follows failure of one duct to form. It is uncommon and often accompanies renal agenesis on the missing side.
w.T-shaped uterus: A T-shaped uterus follows prenatal diethylstilbestrol exposure. It is rare and is not the anomaly most linked to recurrent miscarriage.

pt.say: The third card shows the septate uterus, a persistent midline septum, marked as the most common anomaly and the one linked to recurrent miscarriage.

q: Which kidney anomaly most often accompanies a unicornuate uterus?
x: The ureteric bud arises from the mesonephric duct, which also guides the Müllerian duct. A unicornuate uterus therefore often comes with renal agenesis on the same side as the missing horn.

w.Polycystic kidney disease: Polycystic kidney disease is an inherited disorder of the kidney tubules. It has no shared embryonic origin with the Müllerian ducts.
w.Horseshoe kidney: A horseshoe kidney forms when the lower poles fuse and ascent is blocked. That is a separate event from Müllerian development.
w.Wilms tumor: Wilms tumor is an embryonal kidney cancer of early childhood. It is not linked to Müllerian defects.
w.Renal artery stenosis: Renal artery stenosis is acquired, from fibromuscular dysplasia or atherosclerosis, and causes hypertension. It is not an embryonic defect.

pt.say: The first card pairs a unicornuate uterus, where one duct fails, with ipsilateral renal agenesis, because the mesonephric duct that guides the Müllerian duct also sprouts the ureteric bud.

q: The gubernaculum persists as which ligaments in females?
x: The gubernaculum runs from the gonad to the labioscrotal swelling. In females the uterus interrupts it, leaving the ovarian ligament above and the round ligament below, which passes through the inguinal canal to the labia majora.

w.Broad ligament: The broad ligament is a double fold of peritoneum draped over the uterus and tubes, formed as the Müllerian ducts fuse.
w.Cardinal ligaments: The cardinal ligaments are condensed pelvic fascia at the cervix carrying the uterine vessels. They are not gubernacular remnants.
w.Uterosacral ligaments: Uterosacral ligaments are fascial bands from the cervix to the sacrum that support the uterus, formed from pelvic connective tissue.
w.Suspensory ligaments of the ovary: The suspensory (infundibulopelvic) ligament carries the ovarian vessels from the pelvic wall and marks the ovary's original high position.

pt.say: In the gubernaculum row, the female side reads ovarian and round ligaments; the male side anchors the testis in the scrotum.

q: Which abdominal wall layer gives the spermatic cord its cremaster muscle?
x: As the testis passes the internal oblique it carries muscle fibers that become the cremaster. Contraction lifts the testis in the cremasteric reflex, and the motor supply is the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.

w.External oblique aponeurosis: The external oblique aponeurosis gives the outermost covering, the external spermatic fascia, at the superficial inguinal ring.
w.Transversalis fascia: The transversalis fascia gives the innermost covering, the internal spermatic fascia, at the deep inguinal ring.
w.Parietal peritoneum: The parietal peritoneum provides the processus vaginalis, whose remnant becomes the tunica vaginalis around the testis itself.
w.Scarpa fascia: Scarpa fascia continues into the perineum as Colles fascia and the dartos layer of the scrotum. It does not wrap the cord.

pt.say: In the coverings panel the internal oblique muscle gives the cremaster muscle and fascia, while the external oblique aponeurosis gives the external spermatic fascia.

q: Which peritoneal pouch becomes the tunica vaginalis?
x: The processus vaginalis is an outpouching of peritoneum that precedes the testis through the inguinal canal. Its distal part stays as the tunica vaginalis, and a patent proximal part allows indirect hernias and communicating hydroceles.

w.Gubernaculum: The gubernaculum is the solid mesenchymal cord that guides the testis downward. It becomes a scrotal ligament, not a serous sac.
w.Tunica albuginea: The tunica albuginea is the dense fibrous capsule of the testis itself, formed from gonadal mesenchyme beneath the tunica vaginalis.
w.Dartos fascia: The dartos is smooth muscle in the scrotal subcutaneous tissue that wrinkles the skin for temperature control. It is not peritoneum.
w.Rectovesical pouch: The rectovesical pouch is the lowest peritoneal recess in the male pelvis, between bladder and rectum, far from the scrotum.

pt.say: The last row of the figure shows the processus vaginalis becoming the tunica vaginalis in males.

q: Where do primordial germ cells arise before migrating to the gonad?
x: Primordial germ cells arise in the wall of the yolk sac and migrate to the genital ridge during weeks 4 to 6. Without them the gonad fails to develop normally.

w.Genital ridge: The genital ridge is the destination, a strip of intermediate mesoderm beside the mesonephros that provides the supporting cells, not the germ cells.
w.Mesonephric duct: The mesonephric duct drains the embryonic kidney and becomes the male genital ducts. It lies lateral to the gonad and makes no gametes.
w.Neural crest: Neural crest cells migrate to form ganglia, melanocytes and the adrenal medulla, but gametes have a separate, earlier lineage.
w.Primitive streak: The primitive streak is where epiblast cells ingress to form mesoderm and endoderm in week 3. It is not where germ cells gather.

hl: germ cells from the yolk sac
pt.say: The top band of the figure notes germ cells from the yolk sac joining the genital ridge gonad in the indifferent stage.
